title: Dynamic Programming State and Transition
summary: Represent each reusable subproblem with the smallest state that preserves everything future decisions need, then compute that state's answer from smaller states.
recognition_signals: a recursive formulation revisits the same logical subproblems
different choice histories can lead to the same future problem
the answer can be expressed from smaller already-defined states
core_rules: Two histories may share one DP state only when their future options and required result are identical.
A transition must read only states whose answers are already defined by recursion plus memoization or by a valid tabulation order.
structural_steps: write the recurrence from smaller states
cache states on demand or compute them in dependency order

common_confusions.distinction: Backtracking explores histories separately. DP merges histories that reach the same future-relevant state.
DP is appropriate when competing choices create future trade-offs and no one local choice is known to be safe.
